thesis: The author argues that while selling appreciated assets to realize gains is a common psychological impulse to avoid regret, it does not necessarily make sense to sell solely because an asset has increased in value. Conversely, the author contends that selling assets simply because they have declined is even worse, as widespread selling of down assets can turn market declines into crashes.
